distinctions_recorded: TWO DIALS, NOT A DUPLICATION. chart's dial measures WHICH STRATUM ANSWERED (floor/tree/claude — a COMPILATION metric: is the boundary moving down). learning_block's dial measures AKIEN'S GATE BEHAVIOUR (firings, send_backs, approvals, match_rate — a DELEGATION metric: can this gate be handed off). Different axes, neither terminal. Measured this session: cairn/machines/chart/ contains zero references to learning_block.

TWO STORES, DIFFERENT OBJECTS. chart trees hold CONTENT (what was decided about this class of request); learning traces hold BEHAVIOUR (did the door refuse, did the gate approve). This is NOT a second write path into CairnCommons/learning/ — learning_block's falsifier (7) is not tripped.

'/intent DOESN'T FILE TO COMMONS' IS NOT VIOLATED. That rule exists so an UNRESOLVED NODE is not filed as though resolved. A verdict record is not the node — it is the record of the firing. Recorded explicitly because it reads as a contradiction at a glance and a future reader will trip on it.

A SKILL'S DOOR CANNOT BE PHYSICS BY BEING CALLED. The executor of a skill is an LLM reading markdown, so a door the markdown ASKS to be called can be skipped or fed a shaped payload — the exact skate the parent ticket exists to close. Cairn already solved this for LLM-executed steps and NOT by trust: (a) the stage gate refuses a malformed packet, (b) the next stage template-fills from the previous berth so skipping is a build error, (c) a downstream consumer refuses to proceed without the artifact (the emit chokepoint's EntryGateRed). This ticket APPLIES that proven pattern rather than inventing skill-migration machinery — which is also what makes 'template brick' a strong claim: the pattern has already survived nine instances.

THE MOST VALUABLE FIRING IS THE ONE THAT VANISHES TODAY. /intent has TWO exits: routed-forward, and routed-OUT (nothing traces to the Telos, so the node dies here). The kill is the cheapest win in the system — an intention that shouldn't exist, stopped before any cost — and it is the one exit with NO downstream artifact to record it. It currently vanishes into conversation. This single case justifies the trace organ better than any argument brought into the pass; it is why 'finding at BOTH exits' is in the intention and not an afterthought.

THE SKILLS ARE IN GIT. Measured this session: ~/.claude/skills/* are SYMLINKS into skills/<name>/ (same inode). A skill is therefore a proper code-seam-shaped node with one code address that can carry state/history beside it (skills/sail/ already does) — NOT a host-seam whose implementation git cannot see. This is what makes the class assignment 'skill' rather than 'host-seam' a measured call.

THIS TICKET CANNOT CARRY THE BERTH IT MANDATES. /intent was fired on this very node (dogfooding: the first act of migrating /intent is firing it), but the berth mechanism is what this ticket BUILDS — so the firing exists in conversation only. The chicken-and-egg is named here rather than papered over; the gate's first real subject is the ticket AFTER this one.

Whether /intent needs new shell verbs or an inline python step is a build decision, not a design one — but it is the reason child b touches the primitive at all.
